transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

In class and in the hospital, I keep jumping in and answering or talking before people even finish their questions, and it’s getting me into trouble. I'm really stressed because it's putting my spot in my radiology program at risk.

Have you had this tendency to blurt things out or act before thinking since childhood, or did it mainly start after the recent stress in your radiology program? Outside of this stressful period, do you also have ongoing problems with attention or restlessness in other settings?

It actually goes way back to elementary school; my teachers always sent notes home about me getting out of my seat, blurting out answers, and having a hard time waiting my turn. It's definitely not just at school either, because even at home I can't sit still to watch a movie with my family, and I get incredibly restless just waiting in everyday lines.

Besides blurting things out and feeling restless, do you also often have trouble staying focused, finishing tasks, or organizing things at work or home? Has this been a long-term pattern in more than one setting?

Focusing and organizing tasks isn't really my main issue, because my technical and artistic work actually goes quite well once I'm doing it. However, the restlessness and interrupting have definitely been a long-term pattern since elementary school, and it affects me at school, the hospital, and even at home when trying to relax with my family.

Have you also had a long-term pattern of serious rule-breaking or aggressive behavior, like fighting, bullying, destroying property, stealing, or repeatedly lying? Or is the main problem mostly impulsivity and restlessness without those behaviors?

No, I've never been aggressive or broken rules like that, and I've always tried my best to follow the rules and avoid trouble since I was a kid. My struggles are entirely about my physical restlessness, impatience, and impulsively blurting things out before I can stop myself. I'm definitely not trying to cause trouble on purpose.

Symptoms cause clear functional impairment in training/work.
